hypothesis: With arrival pacing matched in the no-pause control, a fixed-worker closed-loop load generator will understate p99 latency by at least twofold and falsely pass a 100 ms SLO in at least 75% of repeats when rare global service pauses suppress scheduled arrivals, while an interval-corrected histogram will move toward the open-loop estimate.
claimBoundary: The evidence supports a measurement-bias claim for the declared single-server FCFS simulation with scheduled pauses. It cannot establish a universal correction, production model-server capacity, continuous-batching behavior, or the performance of any named load generator.

baselines: Open-loop Poisson arrivals at the declared target request rate
Naive fixed-worker closed-loop load generation at the same nominal rate
controls: No-pause negative control at 80 requests per second
Rare 400 ms pause ablation at 80 requests per second
Bursty 800 ms pause cells at 80 and 100 requests per second
Expected-interval histogram correction as a diagnostic rather than an oracle
